commitResults.messageTitle: Add the role to the Person model and data file
commitResults.messageBody: A person may now carry one of the three client roles, or no role at all. The role is stored under the role key as its lowercase token, and the key is left out entirely when there is no role, so files saved before this change still load. Commands that rebuild a person carry the existing role over, so editing a remark or a phone number does not erase it.

commitResults.messageBody:
The window minimum is too narrow for two panes and too tall for

Set the minimum width to 820 and height to 440 so both panes have
room while the window can fit shorter screens.

Refs #88

commitResults.messageBody:
The detail placeholder is blank and gives no guidance about its
purpose. Users need a clear indication of what belongs in that space.

Show a selection prompt to explain the purpose of the detail pane.
Keep the message readable within the available space.

Refs #88

commitResults.messageTitle: Focus the command box when the app opens
commitResults.messageBody:
The expanded window introduces additional focusable controls.
Users should be able to start typing commands immediately.

Focus the command input after the window has finished loading so
users can begin without clicking the field. Add a startup UI test
to guard this behaviour.

Refs #88

commitResults.messageTitle: Test the main window at supported layout sizes
commitResults.messageBody:
The two-pane window must remain usable when display scaling
reduces the available space. Layout changes could otherwise hide
controls or overlap the footer.

Add an automated check for the effective layout sizes in issue #88
and the minimum window size. Verify that the main regions fit,
pane widths are preserved, and footer labels do not overlap.

These checks simulate available layout space rather than native
operating-system display scaling.

Refs #88

commitResults.messageTitle: Restructure client cards into three rows
commitResults.messageBody:
Client cards spread contact details across several lines and repeat
the address, making the list harder to scan.

Group the index, name and role above a shared phone and email row,
with tags underneath. Remove the address from the card without
changing stored client data.

Constrain long name and email text so role badges remain visible
in narrow lists. Add UI tests for the field layout and text overflow.

Refs #95

commitResults.messageTitle: Keep client cards at a consistent compact height
commitResults.messageBody:
Cards shrink when tags are absent and grow when tags wrap, so the
list cannot maintain a predictable density on small screens.

Keep the base card height at 70 pixels and fit tags on one row.
Show a count and tooltip for tags that do not fit, restoring tags
as more space becomes available.

Add tests for optional fields, tag overflow, layout stability and
three complete cards in a compact list. These are layout checks,
not native operating-system display-scaling verification.

Refs #95

commitResults.messageTitle: Use singular wording for one displayed client
commitResults.messageBody:
The footer uses a plural label even when only one client is displayed.
This produces the grammatical error '1 clients' during normal use.

Show '1 client' for a count of one and retain 'clients' for all other
counts. Update the add, find and delete UI checks to guard the wording.

Refs #88

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge master and address main window review
commitResults.messageBody:
The main window branch conflicts with the merged clear-confirmation
tests. Its layout test also implies display-scaling coverage that it
does not provide.

The branch needs the latest team changes without losing either set of
tests or claiming unverified display-scaling results.

Merge master while preserving both sets of tests. Require confirmation
before checking an empty footer, assert the placeholder text, and add
manual display-scaling instructions with results left unverified.

Refs #88
Restructure the main window into list and detail panes

The tag container is a StackPane, but its stylesheet still declares
FlowPane-only gap properties.

These unused rules suggest that CSS controls spacing even though
TagRow owns the layout.

Remove the obsolete gap rules while retaining the tag-label styles
so the stylesheet matches the compact card implementation.

Refs #95

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge master and verify compact card integration
commitResults.messageBody:
The card branch predates the two-pane main window. Its compact-layout
test only exercises the list in isolation.

The redesign needs a regression check against the complete window
and the latest team changes.

Merge master and add a full-window check at 853 by 480 logical pixels.
Verify three complete 70-pixel cards with long text and missing tags,
alongside the detail prompt and live footer count.

Keep this check distinct from actual operating-system display scaling,
which remains unverified in #123.
